title: The Dragons of Eden
author: Carl Sagan
description: The Dragons of Eden: Speculations on the Evolution of Human Intelligence by Carl Sagan (Random House, 1977), winner of the 1978 Pulitzer Prize for General Non-Fiction. Sagan, the astronomer and science communicator, combines evolutionary biology, neuroscience, anthropology and computer science to ask how human intelligence evolved. He uses the 'cosmic calendar' to compress the history of the universe into a year, discusses the information content of genes and brains, and draws on Paul MacLean's triune brain model (the reptilian R-complex, limbic system and neocortex) to explore aggression, ritual, emotion and reason. Further chapters cover the split brain and the two hemispheres, chimpanzee language studies, dreams, the Eden myth as a memory of the emergence of consciousness, and the future of artificial and extraterrestrial intelligence. It is a classic of popular science on the evolution of mind.
